R2.note: data buffer; pin numbering differs if AM83048 fitted

D12.note: X DAC latch. Earlier read gave 'Q11' as the alternate designator; sheet 02B shows Q11 is a 2N6044 coin-counter driver, so that alternate was a misread and has been withdrawn.

F10.note: drawing cites this exact chip as the revision example

notes: ROM/PROM substitution table: ROM 035127 at N/P3; PROM 035129 at K4, 035130 at L4, with a split pad bridged at K/L3.

Revision pairs are a one-position shift: the -05/-06 board moves a designator up one row from the -01 thru -04 board (D8->D9, D9->D10, C9->C10, J8->J9). Any build must declare which revision it describes.
Revision convention confirmed verbatim on the drawing: red designators are for -05/-06 assemblies; the LS174 example is F10 on -01 thru -04 and F11 on -05/-06.

Sheet 01A is the Video Power Supply wiring diagram (034633-01) — cabinet wiring, no game-board ICs. Sheet 01B is the microcomputer: clock, reset, watchdog. Designators are board-wide across sheets: D4/LS74, B5/LS04, B6/LS14 and C6/LS00 appear identically on 01B and 02A, which independently corroborates the sheet 2A reading.
Sheet 02B is Inputs/Outputs: player input muxes and the sound section (555 thump oscillator, 566 VCO for the saucer). Text references N7 (sound bit code) and M10 (control-signal latch).
Sheet 01B carries the full memory map: vector RAM 4000-47FF, vector ROM 5000-57FF, program 6800-7FFF, with switch and sound registers from 2003 to 3E00.
Program ROMs are Atari-numbered 035131-035135 at J2, N2, H2, M2, F2; further ROM positions run off the right of this crop and are not yet read.

Board assembly numbers are 034986-01 thru -06; sheet 01B is rev H for -01 thru -04 and rev B for -05/-06. There is no single 'Asteroids board': the program memory alone has four distinct configurations, so boards/asteroids.json must target one named revision.
conflicts: C8 reads as 82S129 (state-machine PROM, Atari 034002) in the state machine block and as an LS02 in the -06-only PROM block. Both cannot hold for one revision; needs resolving against a specific board.

L8: read as a 74LS42 decoder on sheet 2A, but sheet 01B's power text names 'operational amplifiers P11 and L8' in the audio output. One of the two is wrong, or the designator is reused across board areas. Needs a physical board.

C3.note: Atari 90-6013. Drawing warns: MPU runs at 1.5MHz so it MUST be a 6502A; a plain 6502 tops out at 1MHz and is not compatible.

B2.note: address buffer; split pads allow an LS245 substitution

J2.note: program memory, -03 PROM configuration only — see memory_by_revision

N2.note: program memory, -03 PROM configuration only — see memory_by_revision

H2.note: program memory, -03 PROM configuration only — see memory_by_revision

M2.note: program memory, -03 PROM configuration only — see memory_by_revision

F2.note: program memory, -03 PROM configuration only — see memory_by_revision

C5.note: NMI counter; divides 3kHz by 12, interrupt every 4ms

J10.note: coin door / control panel mux, SINP1

P11.note: audio mixer; all sounds mixed in 1/4 of P11

N11.note: 74LS174 hex flip-flop shared across functions: coin-counter latch on sheet 02B and the RAMSEL latch on 01B. Different bits of one package, not a conflicting reading.

D11.note: X axis; text: 'the DACs (D11 and B11)'

corrections: sheet2A D12: alternate designator 'Q11' withdrawn — Q11 is a transistor on sheet 02B. Caught by cross-sheet checking, not by re-reading the same sheet.

memory_by_revision.note: The program memory complement is not shifted between revisions, it is entirely different. Read from the substitution table on sheet 01B.

resolved: F8 (rate multiplier vs 035904 PROM) is RESOLVED, and both readings were right. The Asteroids parts list names 'A034986-05 Game PCB Assembly (with 7497 Rate Multipliers)' and 'A034986-06 ... (with PROM)'. The -06 board replaces the rate multipliers with PROMs, which is exactly what the '-06 PCB ONLY' block on the drawing shows. Confirmed from a different document entirely.
